title: What If You Flew Fast Enough to Chase the Sun?

scenes.text: What if you flew west fast enough to chase the Sun? Planes once did it.
Earth spins at about 1,037 miles an hour at the equator.
Farther north it's slower. At 45 degrees latitude, the ground moves about 733 miles an hour.
Concorde cruised at 1,336 miles an hour. Flying west, it outran the Sun's apparent motion.
The sunset would stall, and the Sun would seem to hang in the sky.
Even better, Concorde left London at 10:30 a.m. and landed in New York at 9:25 a.m. local time, about three and a half hours later.
